name: Lindow Man

attributes.attribute: a bog body found near Lindow town in Britain
died the threefold death of Irish legend
a Celtic rite of a triple way of dying

sources: Ross, Anne. “Lindow Man and the Celtic Tradition.” In The Lindow Man: The Body in the Bog, edited by I. M. Stead, J. B. Bourke, and Don Brothwell, 162–169. Ithaca, N.Y.: Cornell University Press, 1986.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Lindow Man is a ritual find from Celtic Britain. In 1984 workers digging for peat found a body in a bog near the town of Lindow. The water had kept the body whole. The dead man had met the threefold death of Irish legend. Some read him as a human sacrifice or as an offering to end famine or plague. Either way the find is a real artifact of ancient belief.

okr.objective: Record the Lindow Man as a real find of Celtic belief.
key_results: Give the place and year of the find.
State the death and its reading as a sacrifice.
